newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks surge on lower unemployment data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks surge on lower unemployment data.

text.p: Mexican stocks sharply extended initial gains in late morning trade on Thursday as lower-than-expected unemployment data gave buyers a shot in the arm, dealers said.
"The unemployment data went down really well, the market is in full flight and looks like chalking up new records," a floor trader said.

The leading IPC share index was up 80.04 points, or 1.67 percent, at 4,867.47. Mexico's National Statistics Institute announced Mexico's open unemployment rate had fallen to 3.4 percent in June from 3.9 percent in May.
Traders said falling unemployment helped confirm the economy is recovering.
Favorable second quarter earnings so far have also driven players to buy as they seemed to indicate a long-awaited recovery in consumption, traders said.
"Soriana's earnings were well received and the retail sector looks good," the trader added.
Retailer Organizacin Soriana posted first half net earnings in early trade that were up 19 percent in real year-on-year terms. The share was meanwhile up 95 centavos to 25.55 pesos.
Volume had recovered from a moderate start to a brisk 70.4 million shares.
The broad market balance was strongly towards gainers, which outnumbered sliders by 59 to 19 out of a total of 97 stocks that changed hands.
On Wall Street, the Dow Jones industrial average declined 18.11 points to 8.020.77.

The Bovespa index of most active stocks in Sao Paulo meanwhile fell sharply again, ending down 7.22 percent to 11,728 points. However, the decline in Brazil did not trigger jitters in Mexico as it had done on Tuesday, dealers said.

Buyers had driven up share prices in early trade after the National Statistics Institute said June's open unemployment rate was 3.4 percent, or well below the 3.92 percent predicted in the latest Reuters survey of Mexico City financial firms MEX22.

"The (unemployment) data were just great, they underpin improvements in the economy," said Gerardo Copca, an analyst at the Finamex brokerage, who added that several early second quarter earnings reports had also encouraged buyers.
"The results are living up to expectations," he said.
Retail chain Soriana posted a 19-percent increase in real net earnings for the first half in early trade, compared to the year-ago quarter.
Dealers said profit-taking was most notable in Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) and beverage company Fondo Economico Mexicano (Femsa).
Telmex closed down 15 centavos at 20.50 pesos, while its ADRs followed suit by declining 3/8 to 51-7/8.
Profit-takers trimmed Femsa by 70 centavos to 52.30 pesos. Traders said Femsa began to slide after a hefty cross-trade in the stock.
Dealers said financial stocks withstood profit-taking best and were in demand up to the close as falling secondary market rates provided an improved outlook for past-due loans problems.
Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial firms, rose 22 centavos to 4.60 pesos.
Trading volume was heavy at 153.2 million shares.
On the broad market, gains stayed ahead of profit-taking and outpaced slides 61 to 40 on 120 stocks traded.
(( --Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
